newsitem.title: USA: Companies to clean fouled Indiana railyard.
newsitem.headline: Companies to clean fouled Indiana railyard.

text.p: Two railroad companies agreed to complete a $25 million cleanup of dangerous chemicals that fouled soil and groundwater at a railyard and surrounding areas in Elkhart, Ind., the Justice Department said Tuesday.

Under the deal, Pennsylvania-based Consolidated Rail Corporation, a subsidiary of Conrail Inc, and Ohio-based Penn Central Corporation are to finish cleaning the railyard and reimburse the U.S. government for more than $7 million in cleanup costs.

Penn Central, a former railroad company now owned by Ohio-based American Premier Underwriters, ran the railroad yard until 1976, when the site was transferred to Conrail. Conrail is in the process of being bought by two other railroads, CSX Corp and Norfolk Southern Corp.

As part of the cleanup, businesses and homes in the area are being provided with alternative water after a number of wells that provide drinking water were found to be tainted with hazardous substances, including suspected carcinogens.
The agreement in U.S. District Court in Indiana settles the government's claims against the companies, filed under the Superfund hazardous waste law.
